question: Who was India's first-ever gold medallist at the Asian Games?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sachin Nag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sachin Nag** was India's first-ever gold medallist at the **Asian Games**.
 
• He achieved this feat in the inaugural Asian Games held in **1951** in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• Sachin Nag won the gold medal in the **100-meter freestyle swimming event**, marking a historic moment for Indian sports.
 
• The 1951 Asian Games were hosted by India and featured participants from multiple Asian countries, making it a significant event in the region's sports history.
 
• His victory was a proud achievement that highlighted India's emerging talent in international sports post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Asian Games (1951):**

 
 
• The **Asian Games** were held for the first time in **1951** in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• The event was inaugurated by then Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• A total of **11 countries** participated in the games, competing in **57 events across 8 sports**.
 
• India ranked **second** in the medal tally, winning a total of **51 medals** (15 gold, 16 silver, and 20 bronze).
 
 
 
• **Sachin Nag’s Contribution:**
 
 
• Sachin Nag was a prominent swimmer and is considered one of the pioneers of Indian swimming.
 
• His victory in the 100-meter freestyle was a significant achievement during a period when India was striving to establish itself on the global sports stage.
 
• He not only set an example for future athletes but also brought attention to aquatic sports in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Indian Athletes at the 1951 Asian Games:**
 
 
• India performed exceptionally well, with athletes winning medals in disciplines like athletics, wrestling, and field hockey.
 
• Indian hockey team clinched the gold medal, continuing its dominance in international hockey.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Asian Games:**
 
 
• The Asian Games have grown significantly since their inception, becoming one of the premier sporting events in the region.
 
• India has remained an active participant, consistently contributing to the event’s success.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **KD Jadhav:**

 
 
• KD Jadhav was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic medal (bronze in wrestling) at the **1952 Helsinki Olympics**, but he did not win a medal at the Asian Games.
 
 
 
• **PT Usha:**
 
 
• PT Usha is one of India's most celebrated athletes, famously known as the "Payyoli Express." She excelled in athletics during the **1982 Asian Games** and subsequent editions but is not related to the 1951 games.
 
 
 
• **Kanti Shah:**
 
 
• Kanti Shah is not associated with sports or the Asian Games. His name might be included erroneously in the context of this question.
